preamble: Denasalization of [ũ] to oral [u] is a stage in the Galician-Portuguese loss of intervocalic n: Latin lūna first became lũa with the nasality transferred to the vowel, and the nasal vowel was later denasalized, giving Portuguese lua and Galician lúa 'moon'.

examples.note: Intervocalic n was lost leaving a nasal vowel, which later lost its nasality; Galician has the cognate lúa.

sources: Williams, E. B. (1962). From Latin to Portuguese (2nd ed.). University of Pennsylvania Press.
